summary: Canyon County, ID 100-foot Aermotor tower on Deer Flat NWR near Nampa; reported built 1937 as a fire lookout; refuge plans removal pending an archaeological review.

facts.status_note: Listed as standing on a July 2024 visit and on the Idaho lookout list, but the refuge plans to take it down; the removal timeline awaits an archaeological review
facts.agency: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, Deer Flat National Wildlife Refuge

access.note: The area behind the refuge headquarters is closed to visitors; the tower is fenced and cannot be climbed. Officials say trespassers still climb it without permission.

visit.trail_note: Viewed from a roadside pullout by the headquarters gate on Lake Avenue in 2024. Viewing only; do not climb.

events.note: Idaho Press says it was initially constructed in 1937 to serve as a fire lookout; the Roaming Civic could not confirm the build date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The lookout list and the July 2024 visit both say standing. The Idaho Press reports a plan to take it down, with no removal done or timeline set in the copy we read. Reported as standing with removal planned.
The Idaho Press gives a 1937 build date and a fire-lookout purpose. The Roaming Civic found no confirmed build date or fire use. The 1937 date is unconfirmed by a second source.

notes_for_editor: The Idaho Press article has no publication date in our cached copy, so the takedown plan's timing is unknown; confirm with the refuge before publishing the fate. The 1937 build date and fire-lookout purpose rest on that one article. Roaming Civic says the tower is not on the NHLR. No staffing or fire history found in the pages read. The Idaho Press fetch returned HTTP 429 on earlier tries and succeeded on a later retry. Brief access 'unknown' is now closed per the 2024 visit.
